User: If I was to imagine somewhere serene to escape from the rat race, somewhere to down the digital tools and properly relax in the most beautiful surroundings I could think of, I don’t think I could imagine anywhere more heavenly than Thyme.
Thyme is nestled within the village of Southrop, deep in the heart of the Cotswolds, with all its English roses, immaculate lawns and Cotswold stone. It is the creation of Caryn Hibbert, owner of nearby Southrop Manor and its sprawling country estate. Whilst the very beautiful main house remains private, Caryn and her family have, over the last 15 years, restored all the farm buildings, a Georgian Rectory nearby and the award-winning Swan Inn over the road to create what is the quintessentially perfect English village retreat.
A celebration of Britishness, Caryn has managed to create a luxurious and modern experience whilst keeping the sense of the history of the buildings intact. The magnificent 17th-century Tithe Barn has been revived without any chi-chi embellishments – soaring ceilings and ancient beams give it a grand yet humble vibe, or there’s the 19th Century Ox Barn, which is set to house the new destination Ox Barn restaurant this November, with its 65ft beams and an original herringbone ceiling. This marks their official launch as a 'Village within a village,' the perfect description of Thyme because it isn't like a hotel in the traditional sense in shape or form.
Thyme feels a million miles away from city life, both physically but also metaphorically speaking, probably because its heart is the land it sits on. So often we’re told that the key to destressing is in getting back to nature and at Thyme there's an abundance of it. There’s a 150-acre farm that provides a rich, healthy soil for abundant vegetable gardens, a herb garden, cutting gardens and polytunnels that are productive all year round. The sprawling grounds supply the spa, the restaurants and the cookery school and every morning, chefs and gardeners meet to discuss what they can pick and create for the day ahead. Then there are the gardens that weave throughout the grounds, brought to life by Bunny Guinness a six-time Chelsea Flower Show Gold Medallist complete with orchards and working gardens too. Every doorway is climbing with roses, every flower bed is bursting with florals, whilst bumble bees and wildlife fill the air and trees that soar high above.
When it comes to the rooms, you either choose to stay in the Farmhouse and the cottages around the courtyard or The Lodge, a Georgian Rectory where I had the luxury of staying the night. Again, the rooms are inspired by the lush surroundings and mine – English Rose – looked out onto the gardens and was painted the most sumptuous shell pink (if you are interested it was Cuisse de Nymphe by naturally pigmented paint company Edward Bulmer, whose earth-friendly paints are used throughout – again another reflection of Caryn’s love of the countryside).
What to do when you’re at Thyme apart from rest? Head to The Baa (there are stools that look like shaggy sheep to sit on) for a cocktail created with cordials, flowers and herbs fresh from the garden and straw blades in the place of plastic mixers (Thyme has a commitment to sustainability and a drive to remove single-use plastics from the site). Or you can book in for a cookery class where you can really experience Thyme’s ‘love of the land’ first hand. These normally start in the gardens where you can harvest some culinary treats before heading to the kitchen for some season-led cooking. Other treats are picturesque walks, picnics, a visit to The Swan Inn Caryn’s award-winning pub across the road and for me, a run to the next village and a long soak in my roll-top pink bath.
But you absolutely can’t leave Thyme without a visit to the Meadow Spa right in the centre of the Thyme nest. A botanical-inspired haven with a chemical-free pool that uses the water from Thyme’s natural underground spring that flows deep below their meadows, the minute I entered the green and white tiled Greenhouse reception (I fell in love with that tiled floor and immediately told my husband we needed a new bathroom), I could immediately feel my shoulders drop. After a drink of botanical-infused water (using herbs from the gardens obviously), I was then shown to my treatment room in Meadow Cottage for an Aurelia Probiotic Skincare Signature Treatment (just for the record, one of my fave skincare brands). Given the refreshingly simple option of ‘shorter facial and more massage' or 'more facial and shorter massage’ I chose more massage. I don’t remember a huge amount about what happened next but I just about recall being pummelled and scrubbed to awake with seriously glowy skin and a much less knotty neck. The following morning I fell out of bed into a super chilled yoga class (which start officially in November too) before wafting into breakfast.
If you’re looking to escape the humdrum of modern life for a night, a weekend or longer, this would be my go-to place to hide away and forget about the outside world. If I were you I’d leave your phone at reception, the experience and being mindful of the surrounding nature is just too good a restorative experience to miss.

User: If I was to imagine somewhere serene to escape from the rat race, somewhere to down the digital tools and properly relax in the most beautiful surroundings I could think of, I don’t think I could imagine anywhere more heavenly than Thyme.
Thyme is nestled within the village of Southrop, deep in the heart of the Cotswolds, with all its English roses, immaculate lawns and Cotswold stone. It is the creation of Caryn Hibbert, owner of nearby Southrop Manor and its sprawling country estate. Whilst the very beautiful main house remains private, Caryn and her family have, over the last 15 years, restored all the farm buildings, a Georgian Rectory nearby and the award-winning Swan Inn over the road to create what is the quintessentially perfect English village retreat.
A celebration of Britishness, Caryn has managed to create a luxurious and modern experience whilst keeping the sense of the history of the buildings intact. The magnificent 17th-century Tithe Barn has been revived without any chi-chi embellishments – soaring ceilings and ancient beams give it a grand yet humble vibe, or there’s the 19th Century Ox Barn, which is set to house the new destination Ox Barn restaurant this November, with its 65ft beams and an original herringbone ceiling. This marks their official launch as a 'Village within a village,' the perfect description of Thyme because it isn't like a hotel in the traditional sense in shape or form.
Thyme feels a million miles away from city life, both physically but also metaphorically speaking, probably because its heart is the land it sits on. So often we’re told that the key to destressing is in getting back to nature and at Thyme there's an abundance of it. There’s a 150-acre farm that provides a rich, healthy soil for abundant vegetable gardens, a herb garden, cutting gardens and polytunnels that are productive all year round. The sprawling grounds supply the spa, the restaurants and the cookery school and every morning, chefs and gardeners meet to discuss what they can pick and create for the day ahead. Then there are the gardens that weave throughout the grounds, brought to life by Bunny Guinness a six-time Chelsea Flower Show Gold Medallist complete with orchards and working gardens too. Every doorway is climbing with roses, every flower bed is bursting with florals, whilst bumble bees and wildlife fill the air and trees that soar high above.
When it comes to the rooms, you either choose to stay in the Farmhouse and the cottages around the courtyard or The Lodge, a Georgian Rectory where I had the luxury of staying the night. Again, the rooms are inspired by the lush surroundings and mine – English Rose – looked out onto the gardens and was painted the most sumptuous shell pink (if you are interested it was Cuisse de Nymphe by naturally pigmented paint company Edward Bulmer, whose earth-friendly paints are used throughout – again another reflection of Caryn’s love of the countryside).
What to do when you’re at Thyme apart from rest? Head to The Baa (there are stools that look like shaggy sheep to sit on) for a cocktail created with cordials, flowers and herbs fresh from the garden and straw blades in the place of plastic mixers (Thyme has a commitment to sustainability and a drive to remove single-use plastics from the site). Or you can book in for a cookery class where you can really experience Thyme’s ‘love of the land’ first hand. These normally start in the gardens where you can harvest some culinary treats before heading to the kitchen for some season-led cooking. Other treats are picturesque walks, picnics, a visit to The Swan Inn Caryn’s award-winning pub across the road and for me, a run to the next village and a long soak in my roll-top pink bath.
But you absolutely can’t leave Thyme without a visit to the Meadow Spa right in the centre of the Thyme nest. A botanical-inspired haven with a chemical-free pool that uses the water from Thyme’s natural underground spring that flows deep below their meadows, the minute I entered the green and white tiled Greenhouse reception (I fell in love with that tiled floor and immediately told my husband we needed a new bathroom), I could immediately feel my shoulders drop. After a drink of botanical-infused water (using herbs from the gardens obviously), I was then shown to my treatment room in Meadow Cottage for an Aurelia Probiotic Skincare Signature Treatment (just for the record, one of my fave skincare brands). Given the refreshingly simple option of ‘shorter facial and more massage' or 'more facial and shorter massage’ I chose more massage. I don’t remember a huge amount about what happened next but I just about recall being pummelled and scrubbed to awake with seriously glowy skin and a much less knotty neck. The following morning I fell out of bed into a super chilled yoga class (which start officially in November too) before wafting into breakfast.
If you’re looking to escape the humdrum of modern life for a night, a weekend or longer, this would be my go-to place to hide away and forget about the outside world. If I were you I’d leave your phone at reception, the experience and being mindful of the surrounding nature is just too good a restorative experience to miss.

Question/Instruction: What is the easiest part of Tom Gustafson's job as a chiropractor, and how does he validate his patients' outcomes?

Given material: Tom Gustafson owns Active Healing Center in Colts Neck.
I decided I want to be an entrepreneur while working as an associate doctor of chiropractic after graduating chiropractic school. I enjoyed my time as an associate doctor, but knew I wanted to run my own practice. I graduated school in 1997, and by 1999 I knew I wanted to go out on my own.
I started my own business because I had a vision as to what I wanted to do with my business and the people I wanted to help and that was not being fulfilled as an associate doctor.
The cost to starting my own business was a challenge.
I would look more into taking over an established practice for someone on the verge of retirement.
The personality trait that helps me the most is I am a laid back and very friendly person so I don’t get overstressed. Sometimes being laid back may not be so helpful, but it’s who I am.
The hardest part of the job is not getting too emotionally attached to your patients and their health. I want everyone to live an awesome, healthy life and I want everyone's outcome to be phenomenal. It gets frustrating when people do not follow through with their care program because I know if they did they would get even better results.
The easiest part is sitting down with someone during their revaluations going over their results and outcomes. We always prove our results with pre- and post-testing. I want people to feel great and at the same time they know their body is truly functioning better.
The biggest surprise is all the ups and downs you can go through running your own business.
I would like to work with more people with overall wellness. I incorporated the wellness program into our office one and a half years ago. It’s a phenomenal program making massive impact on the health of our patients. I want to help more people in this regard.
People should come here because we do over-deliver for our patients.
The community is very friendly and it’s a beautiful area. Colts Neck has that countryside feel yet it's so close the the Shore. It's very cool.
Basically, I'm always in contact. The only way to not be in contact is to leave the country.
I enjoy being with my son more than anything. He is the most important person in my life.

c83-m1.summary: The Tlogo Plantation Resort is a convenient spot for a quick weekend getaway from Semarang.
c83-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: So…What to do on my weekend getaway to Salatiga?
Leave Semarang for 1,5 hours drive to Salatiga, so it makes for a convenient spot for a quick weekend jaunt. We ride past beautiful tropical scenery, crossing the legendary swamp of Rawapening en route to Tuntang.
Tlogo Plantation Resort is a nice place for weekend retreat and not too far from Semarang. There are coffee plantation, swimming pool, fishing pool, and many more here suitable for family outing. There are 4 room types: Family cottages IDR 2700, Cottage IDR 700, Deluxe IDR 600, and Superior IDR 500.
Tlogo Agro Plantation was founded in 1856. Enjoy the fresh air of Tlogo Agro Highland and see the various tropical plants grown here, such as coffee, rubber, mango, banana, avocado, clove, cocoa and guava. Learn about the coffee growing process from the bean to powder using old machinery.
It was at the hotel lobby. They have this souvenir shop here for you to buy something back as memories.
It’s an absolutely charming hotel with a traditional style in a fantastic location.
Our cottage room was beautiful – big and spacious with everything we needed (tea and kettle, phew) and the most fantastic view over the coffee plantation.
Clean bed sheet and pillows for you to sleep on. The mattress is comfortable for a good night sleep.
I was in Room 107, a cottage room, and this room was pretty large and comfortable, spacious enough to walk around. The curtains on the left open up to the coffee plantation.
There’s a bedroom with a separate open concept bathroom. There is also a veranda with some chairs. I spent a lovely time that first night watching a movie. If there had been a mountain view, I probably wouldn’t have wanted to leave my room at all.
Clean toilet and water sink. Toilet paper and fresh towels are provided.
View from my room – it was fairly private because it didn’t seem like anyone walked along that particular path.
In the next morning, we had our breakfast in our room.
I managed to explore the hotel grounds a little on Sunday morning when we had a bit of time to ourselves.
On the walk to the coffee plantation.
This place is awesome! The scenery is interesting as you get into the hills and mountains. The coffee plantation is beautiful. The plantation itself is part of a resort which is interesting to see by itself. This is a great way to go past the beautiful countryside of Java.
We spent our days chit-chatting, laughing, and walking on the resort. It’s pretty crowded in the day. If you’re still with me by this point, I’m impressed. This has turned into an incredibly long blog post, so I’m going to keep it brief.
I’d been expecting the rest of Salatiga to be a bit meh, but it was absolutely charming still! It really is the loveliest town and we saw the most beautiful scenery and views.
One afternoon we walked over to the famous Goa Rong View.
To quote my favourite song of the moment, Be Okay: “When your life is great, celebrate the feeling.” I think I’m getting pretty good at achieving that, at appreciating the present and not always dreaming about the future, but it’s something we all need to work at.

User: So…What to do on my weekend getaway to Salatiga?
Leave Semarang for 1,5 hours drive to Salatiga, so it makes for a convenient spot for a quick weekend jaunt. We ride past beautiful tropical scenery, crossing the legendary swamp of Rawapening en route to Tuntang.
Tlogo Plantation Resort is a nice place for weekend retreat and not too far from Semarang. There are coffee plantation, swimming pool, fishing pool, and many more here suitable for family outing. There are 4 room types: Family cottages IDR 2700, Cottage IDR 700, Deluxe IDR 600, and Superior IDR 500.
Tlogo Agro Plantation was founded in 1856. Enjoy the fresh air of Tlogo Agro Highland and see the various tropical plants grown here, such as coffee, rubber, mango, banana, avocado, clove, cocoa and guava. Learn about the coffee growing process from the bean to powder using old machinery.
It was at the hotel lobby. They have this souvenir shop here for you to buy something back as memories.
It’s an absolutely charming hotel with a traditional style in a fantastic location.
Our cottage room was beautiful – big and spacious with everything we needed (tea and kettle, phew) and the most fantastic view over the coffee plantation.
Clean bed sheet and pillows for you to sleep on. The mattress is comfortable for a good night sleep.
I was in Room 107, a cottage room, and this room was pretty large and comfortable, spacious enough to walk around. The curtains on the left open up to the coffee plantation.
There’s a bedroom with a separate open concept bathroom. There is also a veranda with some chairs. I spent a lovely time that first night watching a movie. If there had been a mountain view, I probably wouldn’t have wanted to leave my room at all.
Clean toilet and water sink. Toilet paper and fresh towels are provided.
View from my room – it was fairly private because it didn’t seem like anyone walked along that particular path.
In the next morning, we had our breakfast in our room.
I managed to explore the hotel grounds a little on Sunday morning when we had a bit of time to ourselves.
On the walk to the coffee plantation.
This place is awesome! The scenery is interesting as you get into the hills and mountains. The coffee plantation is beautiful. The plantation itself is part of a resort which is interesting to see by itself. This is a great way to go past the beautiful countryside of Java.
We spent our days chit-chatting, laughing, and walking on the resort. It’s pretty crowded in the day. If you’re still with me by this point, I’m impressed. This has turned into an incredibly long blog post, so I’m going to keep it brief.
I’d been expecting the rest of Salatiga to be a bit meh, but it was absolutely charming still! It really is the loveliest town and we saw the most beautiful scenery and views.
One afternoon we walked over to the famous Goa Rong View.
To quote my favourite song of the moment, Be Okay: “When your life is great, celebrate the feeling.” I think I’m getting pretty good at achieving that, at appreciating the present and not always dreaming about the future, but it’s something we all need to work at.
The whole experience was such a treat. Based on the passage above, Can you provide a brief summary of the Tlogo Plantation Resort and the activities available for families there?
Assistant: The Tlogo Plantation Resort is a convenient spot for a quick weekend getaway from Semarang. It features a coffee plantation, swimming pool, fishing pool, and more, making it suitable for family outings. There are four room types available, ranging from family cottages to superior rooms. The resort is located in Tlogo Agro Highland, where visitors can enjoy the fresh air and see various tropical plants, including coffee, rubber, mango, banana, avocado, clove, cocoa, and guava. Visitors can learn about the coffee growing process from bean to powder using old machinery. The resort also has a souvenir shop where visitors can purchase memorabilia. The resort's charming traditional style and fantastic location make it an ideal spot for a weekend retreat.
User: Can you recommend any other places to visit in Salatiga besides Tlogo Plantation Resort and Goa Rong View?
Assistant: Yes, there are several other places you can visit in Salatiga besides Tlogo Plantation Resort and Goa Rong View. Here are a few suggestions:

1. Satwika Wacana Christian University: One of the top universities in Salatiga, Satwika Wacana Christian University offers a picturesque campus with beautiful gardens and views. 

2. Bukit Cinta or Love Hill: A romantic spot for couples, Love Hill offers a panoramic view of Salatiga and its surrounding areas. 

3. Mount Merbabu National Park: For nature enthusiasts, a visit to Mount Merbabu National Park is a must. The park offers hiking trails, stunning views, and the opportunity to see wildlife such as deer, monkeys, and birds. 

4. Salatiga City Square: Salatiga City Square is a bustling center of the town, offering various shops, restaurants, and street food stalls. 

5. Telogo Warno Nature Tourism: This nature tourism attraction offers visitors the opportunity to explore a lake surrounded by scenic views of rice paddies and mountains. Activities include fishing, boating, and picnicking. 

Overall, Salatiga has a lot to offer visitors in terms of natural and cultural attractions, and there are plenty of places to explore beyond Tlogo Plantation Resort and Goa Rong View.
User: Can you give me more information about the coffee growing process at Tlogo Plantation Resort?
Assistant: Yes, definitely! At Tlogo Plantation Resort in Salatiga, visitors can learn about the coffee growing process from the bean to powder using old machinery. Here is a brief overview of the process:

1. Planting: Coffee is grown from seedlings or seeds that are planted in nurseries. The seeds are covered with soil and watered regularly until the coffee seedlings grow.

2. Transplanting: After the seedlings are large enough, they are then transplanted to the field where they will be grown.

3. Harvesting: After several years of growth, coffee berries start to appear on the plants. These berries are typically harvested between June and August each year in Indonesia.

4. Processing: After harvesting, the berries are washed and dried before being roasted. The processing stage is where the berries are converted to powder. There are different types of processing methods used for coffee, including sun-drying, wet-process, and dry-process.

At Tlogo Plantation Resort, visitors can see firsthand how the coffee berries are processed using traditional machines. The resort also offers guided tours of the coffee plantation where visitors can learn more about the different methods used to grow and process coffee. At the end of the tour, visitors can try a cup of freshly brewed coffee made from the resort's own beans.

User: Likes:
1. The Long Way Home (0312354355)
2. The Girl in the Ice: A gripping serial killer thriller (Detective Erika Foster crime thriller novel) (Volume 1) (1910751774)
User: Dislikes:
1. Younger Next Year for Women - LARGE PRINT (0739462911)
User: Might Like:
1. Bluebird, Bluebird (0316363294)
User: Likes Review:
1. The Long Way Home: Loved this new addition to the Louise Penny series. Her insights into characters and what motivates them are so moving to read. I bought the novel and the audio but in the end, I just wanted to read the words. Her stories just beg to be savored, lingered over, and enjoyed.
2. The Girl in the Ice: A gripping serial killer thriller (Detective Erika Foster crime thriller novel) (Volume 1): I was looking for something new to read. Saw this on my email from BookBub. Noticed the great reviews. I was not disappointed. What a bargain! Totally enjoyed this story. Can't wait for the next book due out in June.
User: Dislikes Review:
1. Younger Next Year for Women - LARGE PRINT: What a waste of time and money. I wish I could get my money back. It infuriates me to know that I gave any money to these wack jobs. I read the sample and it sounded like an interesting read. Beyond the sample is where you see what they are basing their conclusions on that Eating right and exercising 6 days a week and you'll live longer. DAH!!!! The evolution theory to support your premise, well guys that is just a theory and a stupid one at that.
Other Review:
1. Bluebird, Bluebird: Attica Locke is a talented storyteller and writer. I enjoyed this book as a representation of race relations in rural America, and I enjoy the descriptions of the Texas countryside. To me, this story is best enjoyed as a story more like what Harper Lee would have written. It's too slow-paced as a thriller or as a mystery. The characters are all powerful in their own way, from Geneva Sweet, the older black woman who's been in the area all her life, to Darren Matthews, the younger black Texas Ranger who knows justice is not on his side but fights for it anyway. I lived in the central part of the state for eight years and know that the deep rural areas do have issues with race, but that is not just in Texas. Some of the strong language may offend white readers or white Texans, but I know these kinds of hate killings can and do happen. Locke writes very descriptively, and her style works well for character development.
2. Younger Next Year for Women - LARGE PRINT: Seemed out of date. I could have written this book from magazines, TV, books over the last 20 years. Nothing new here at all.
3. The Long Way Home: Yikes. I tried to write a review of this right after I read it and found I was much too angry. I read the first two or three Gamache books and found them quite interesting -- certainly enough to read this one. But good golly, it's bad -- at least not what I consider good storytelling. And filled with artsy-fartsy b.s. The biggest issue I had was at the end when I, even while rolling my eyes, shouted at Clara "don't go you moron!" Then at Myrna "don't let her go you moron!" And Myrna did, and Clara did, and the consequences were so grave, arguably because Clara had gone. And despite all the guilt that had been flying around the book up to this point, there was no acknowledgement of it whatsoever. On the other hand, I could be me. But I can't possibly recommend this book.
4. The Girl in the Ice: A gripping serial killer thriller (Detective Erika Foster crime thriller novel) (Volume 1): Fantastic start to a new detective series! The Girl in the Ice was absolutely gripping from page one. I loved Detective Erika Foster, who was flawed and also vulnerable but stood her ground. It was refreshing to see the class system and politics being tackled in this way. The plot kept me guessing until the end. I had all sorts of theories but was totally wrong. The ending was very satisfying, and I am so pleased that Robert Bryndza is already writing the next book featuring Erika. Highly recommended! I received a copy via NetGalley in exchange for an unbiased review.
User: Hi there! I've read "The Long Way Home" and I absolutely loved it! The way Louise Penny portrays the characters and their motivations is so captivating. I can't wait to read more from her.
Assistant: That's great to hear! Louise Penny's writing style and character insights are truly remarkable.

User: Hi, I'm looking for some ideas for a weekend getaway. Do you have any suggestions?
Assistant: There are many options for a weekend getaway, but it would be helpful to know what you're interested in. Are you looking for something outdoorsy, or perhaps a city break?
User: Hmm, I think I'd prefer something a bit more relaxing. Maybe a visit to a historic house or something like that.
Assistant: That sounds like a great idea! There are many beautiful historic houses with lovely gardens that you could visit. Are you looking for something in a specific location, or are you open to suggestions?
User: I'm pretty open to suggestions. What are some popular options?
Assistant: Well, there are many to choose from, but some popular ones include Chatsworth House, Blenheim Palace, and Highclere Castle. They all have beautiful gardens and a lot of history.
User: Those all sound great, but I think I'm looking for something a bit more... authentic, I suppose. Somewhere that really feels like a step back in time.
Assistant: In that case, you might be interested in visiting some of the lesser-known aristocratic estates. They often have a more intimate feel and can be a great way to experience what life was like in the past.
User: That sounds perfect. I've always had a bit of a fascination with the way the aristocracy lived, and I love exploring old houses and gardens.
Assistant: Well, in that case, I think I can suggest some places that would be right up your alley. But can you tell me a bit more about what specifically interests you about aristocratic estates? Is it the history, the architecture, or something else?
User: To be honest, I think it's the combination of everything. I love the way the houses and gardens were designed to work together, and the way they reflect the personalities of the people who lived there. This person has a keen interest in aristocratic estates and their gardens.
Assistant: It sounds like you have a real passion for the subject. If you're interested in learning more, I would recommend visiting some of the estates that are still lived in by the families who built them. You can get a real sense of the history and tradition that surrounds these places.
User: That's a great idea. Can you suggest some specific places that I might be interested in visiting?
Assistant: Definitely. One place that comes to mind is Castle Howard in Yorkshire. It's a beautiful estate with an incredible garden, and it's still lived in by the Howard family, who built it in the 18th century.
User: That sounds amazing. I'll definitely add it to my list. Do you have any other suggestions?
Assistant: Another place you might be interested in visiting is Houghton Hall in Norfolk. It's a stunning estate with a beautiful garden, and it's still lived in by the Marquess of Cholmondeley. The house and garden are full of interesting historical artifacts and features.
User: Great, I'll make a note of that one too. Thanks for all the suggestions!

User: Not yet, I was about to start looking into it. Do you have any suggestions?
Assistant: There are many online tools that can help you plan your route. But before we dive into that, are you concerned about any aspect of the trip, such as accommodations or expenses?
User: Actually, I am a bit worried about the expenses. It seems like everything is getting more expensive these days.
Assistant: That's a valid concern. Gas prices, in particular, can add up quickly on a long road trip. Have you checked the current gas prices?

User: Those all sound amazing, but I think I'd prefer to visit a lesser-known estate. Something with beautiful gardens and a more intimate atmosphere.
